rationale: The Court will likely issue a tight AEDPA/party-presentation opinion faulting the Fourth Circuit for reframing an exhausted Strickland/Remmer-investigation claim into a freestanding impartial-jury/structural-error theory and for failing to apply claim-specific § 2254(d) deference under Marshall and Shoop. Roberts is best positioned to write a narrow, institutional opinion (with Kavanaugh or Kagan as plausible alternatives), while separate concurrences are most likely from Thomas (textual AEDPA emphasis) and Sotomayor (to stress the Strickland–juror-taint linkage while agreeing AEDPA constrains relief).
